Buyer and seller guides

Buying or selling on the Coast, step by step

Buying or selling a home works about the same way everywhere, but a few things are different on the Mississippi Gulf Coast. Flood zones, wind coverage and the state's disclosure form can change what a home really costs and how long it takes to close. These guides walk through each step in plain English.

What's different on the Coast

Three things to know before you start

  • Flood zonesEvery address has a FEMA flood zone. If a home is in a high-risk zone (one starting with A or V) and you have a federally backed mortgage, your lender will require flood insurance. A regular homeowners policy doesn't cover flooding from rising water.Look up a flood zone on FEMA's map ↗ (opens in a new tab)
  • Wind and hurricane coverageNear the water, many homeowners policies carry a separate hurricane or named-storm deductible, often a percentage of the home's insured value instead of a flat dollar amount. When private companies won't cover wind, the state's wind pool (the Mississippi Windstorm Underwriting Association) offers wind and hail coverage in the coastal counties through local insurance agents.Mississippi Insurance Department ↗ (opens in a new tab)
  • The seller's disclosureMississippi requires most sellers of homes with one to four units to fill out a Property Condition Disclosure Statement. It asks about the roof, water damage, past flooding from rising water and whether the home is in a FEMA flood hazard zone.Mississippi Real Estate Commission ↗ (opens in a new tab)

These guides are general information about buying and selling homes in Mississippi, last reviewed November 2026. It is not legal, tax or insurance advice, and laws, forms, programs and insurance rules change. For advice about your situation, talk with a Mississippi real estate attorney, a tax professional or a licensed insurance agent.

Bill Temple and his brokerage are committed to equal housing opportunity. Every buyer is welcome to look at homes anywhere, and every seller's home is marketed to everyone.
